children: Australians are nervous about the risk of a coming recession, given that inflation remains elevated despite rising unemployment. Still, the alarm might be misplaced, says Jonathan Kearns, chief economist Challenger. Australia is more likely to have a recession when other countries like the U.S. are also in recession, he says. Economic models indicate the probability of a recession in the U.S. is just over 10%, he adds. The same models suggest the likelihood of a recession in Australia is low. But with the Reserve Bank of Australia needing to keep policy tight for some time to squash high inflation, there is always the risk it squeezes too hard, he adds.
